title: Explicit tenant binding authority for shared agent and workflow grants

phases.objective: Permit workspace grants for shared canonical agents and workflows only when the global resource exists and the requested tenant has a current explicit direct allow binding in Dynamic Container authority, without treating availability catalogs, share/delegate intents, or legacy projections as ownership authority.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Workspace resource grant creation for resource_type agent or workflow
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The global canonical resource resolves exactly once and is active, then at least one current direct allow tenant-scoped container_resource_bindings row proves explicit tenant authority before the grant write can continue.
steps: Resolve an agent directly from the global agents registry or a workflow by workflow_id/workflow_key from the global workflows registry.
Reject missing, inactive, or ambiguous global resources before consulting tenant bindings.
Normalize workflow grants to the canonical workflow_key while accepting a direct allow binding recorded against the canonical key or workflow_id.

Require a current active container_resource_bindings row for the requested tenant, active container, active dimension, matching agents/workflows dimension and agent/workflow resource type, with effect=allow.
Do not treat share or delegate bindings as direct workspace-grant authority because Dynamic Container resolution requires their relationship and operation context separately.
Accept multiple valid direct allow bindings for one tenant/resource because they represent multiple authorized container placements rather than resource identity ambiguity.
Reject an active global resource with no current explicit direct allow tenant binding as workspace_resource_reference_unverifiable.
Exercise the resolver contract without connecting to or mutating a live database.
assertions: Activation catalog cross-joins are availability/readback surfaces and are never accepted as tenant ownership authority.
Legacy Dynamic Container projection does not become grant authority merely because it projects workflow context; an explicit direct allow container resource binding is required.
Agent lifecycle authority comes from agents.status=active; transient health_status does not redefine ownership identity.
Workflow lifecycle is active when canonical active/status fields satisfy the repository active-value contract.
Binding eligibility is tenant-scoped, current, active, attached to an active tenant container and active dimension, and requires effect=allow.
Share and delegate effects are excluded from this direct grant-authority shortcut and must continue through their relationship-aware Dynamic Container resolution semantics.
Multiple valid direct allow tenant bindings are allowed while multiple canonical resource identities fail closed as ambiguous.
No Migration Apply, SQL mutation, Production/provider mutation, deployment, credential or secret access, force push, or external send occurs in CI.
